chunks: Hadith 5017 — Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf narrated from Al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said:

A man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed adultery, so purify me.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام turned his face away from him, then said to him: “Sit down.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام turned to the people and said: “Is any one of you incapable, when he commits this evil deed, of concealing it upon himself just as Allah has concealed it for him?” The man stood and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed adultery, so purify me.” He said: “What led you to say what you said?” He replied: “Seeking purification.” He said: “And what purification is better than tawbah (repentance)?”

Then he turned to his companions, speaking to them. The man stood again and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed adultery, so purify me.” He said to him: “Do you recite anything from the Qur'an?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Recite.” So he recited and was correct. He said to him: “Do you know what is obligatory upon you of the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in your salat (prayer) and zakat?” He said: “Yes.” So he questioned him and he answered correctly. He said to him: “Do you have any illness that overtakes you, or do you feel pain in your head, or something in your body, or distress in your chest?” He said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, no.” He said: “Woe to you, go until we inquire about you privately as we questioned you publicly; and if you do not return to us, we will not seek you.” He said: So he inquired about him and was informed that he was sound in condition, and that there was nothing there by which suspicion could enter regarding him.

He said: Then the man returned to him and said to him: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed adultery, so purify me.” He said to him: “Had you not come to us, we would not have sought you out; and we are not ones to leave you alone once the ruling of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has become binding upon you.” Then he said: “O company of people, it suffices that those of you who are present carry out his stoning on behalf of those who are absent. So I adjure by Allah that any man among you who comes tomorrow must veil himself with his turban so that none of you recognizes another, and come to me in the darkness before dawn so that none of you looks at another; for we do not look into the face of a man while we stone him with stones.”

He said: So the people came in the morning as he had instructed them, before the dawn had fully brightened. Then ʿAlī عليه السلام came to them and said: “I adjure by Allah that any man among you upon whom there is a right like this for Allah should carry it out for Allah, for one whom Allah seeks with the like of it does not exact a right for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by it.” He said: So by Allah, a group departed and to this hour we do not know who they were. Then he cast four stones at him, and the people cast at him.

key_terms.التَّوْبَةِ: Tawbah (repentance); presented as the best form of purification.
key_terms.بِالْحِجَارَةِ: With stones; the means of carrying out the stoning.
key_terms.حُقُوقِ اللَّهِ: The rights of Allah; divine obligations and claims upon a person.
key_terms.حُكْمُ اللَّهِ: The ruling of Allah; the binding divine legal judgment.
key_terms.رَجْمَهُ: His stoning; the prescribed punishment mentioned here.
key_terms.زَنَيْتُ: I committed adultery; the confessed offense in the narration.
key_terms.صَلَاتِكَ وَزَكَاتِكَ: Your salat (prayer) and zakat; key religious duties used to assess competence.
key_terms.فَطَهِّرْنِي: Purify me; a request for legal expiation through punishment.

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام deal with a person who repeatedly confessed to adultery and asked to be purified?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام repeatedly turned away a man’s self-confession of adultery, urging concealment of sin and affirming that tawbah (repentance) is the best purification. Only after verifying the man’s sanity, religious competence, and persistence in confession did he proceed with the legal ruling, showing both caution in applying hudud and concern for human dignity.
